apiServiceCorsAllowAllHelp:
The local service sends no Access-Control-Allow-Origin by default, so a cross-origin fetch from a web page is blocked at the CORS preflight. Some sites probe for an aria2 service that way and therefore cannot detect FluxDown.
With this on, every origin gets CORS allow headers — the equivalent of aria2's --rpc-allow-origin-all.
Cost: any web page can probe this port and submit download links. Still in effect: takeover and aria2 submissions raise the confirmation dialog; the management API and MCP require the token.

multiNicHelpHint: Click to see when this helps
multiNicHelp:
How it works: the segment connections of one file are bound to different network adapters, so several internet lines fetch data at the same time and their speeds add up.

When it helps: each adapter leads to a different upstream line (home broadband + 5G hotspot, two carriers, or two broadband lines), and the bottleneck is your own uplink bandwidth. When a server rate-limits per IP, each exit also gets its own quota.

When it doesn't: Ethernet and Wi‑Fi on the same router (the same broadband line) share the same bottleneck, so aggregation gains nothing — the engine detects the shared LAN and ignores the duplicate adapter automatically. It also won't help when the server itself lacks bandwidth or limits speed per connection.

How it avoids slowing you down: each adapter is first measured with one real segment connection, then connections are allocated by measured throughput. A slow line only gets work proportional to its capacity, the tail is split by speed ratio, and stalled connections are handed over to other lines immediately. If no usable extra line is found, behavior is exactly the same as with this feature off.

When it stays off: the task uses a proxy, a VPN/TUN virtual adapter is carrying the traffic, the download address is on the local network, or the server doesn't support segmented downloads.

Note: going through a phone hotspot uses cellular data. A few signed links or cloud drives bound to the source IP may reject requests from another exit; a failing adapter is removed from that task. Once enabled, per-adapter connection counts and downloaded bytes appear in the task details "Log" tab.

pluginErrorPackageTooLarge: The plugin package exceeds the 10 MB size limit.
pluginErrorPackageInvalid: Invalid plugin package: the manifest, script, or version check failed. See the diagnostics log for details.
pluginErrorMarketVersionChanged: The plugin was updated in the marketplace. Review its permissions and install again.
pluginDepsMissingBody: The plugin was installed, but its declared capabilities depend on components that are not installed yet: {components}. Those features stay unavailable until the components are set up. Go to component settings now?
pluginPermConfirmInstallBody: v{version} will be granted the following permissions:
pluginPermConfirmUpdateBody: v{version} requests permissions the installed version does not have:
pluginDetailSettingsCount: {count} field(s), configurable from the plugin card after install
pluginPermFfmpegDesc: Runs FFmpeg for audio/video processing (mux/transcode); requires the FFmpeg component
pluginPermYtdlpDesc: Runs yt-dlp to extract direct media URLs; requires the yt-dlp and FFmpeg components
pluginPermAuthDesc: Stores and reuses this plugin's site credentials, including cookies, Basic, bearer, or custom headers
pluginPermUnknownDesc: Unknown permission (not supported by this version)
pluginDetailUsageBody: Plugins are enabled by default after install and can be toggled in the Installed list at any time. Resolver plugins run automatically before matching downloads start — no manual action needed. Plugins with settings can be configured via the gear button on their card. A plugin that keeps failing is auto-disabled by the circuit breaker. Visit the plugin homepage for detailed usage.
pluginAuthDescription: The plugin drives QR-code login. Scan with the platform app and the system checks the login state automatically.
pluginAuthInputPlaceholder: Account, verification code, or other requested input
pluginAuthSuccess: Login successful; credentials will be reused until they expire
pluginAuthInvalidResponse: The plugin returned an invalid login response
pluginHelperScriptCopied: Script copied. Paste and run it in the site's DevTools console
taskIgnorePluginRetryMsg: This task failed while a plugin was resolving it. Ignoring will skip the plugin and retry with the original link directly. If this keeps happening, check the plugin's settings under Settings → Extensions → Plugins.
pluginAutoDisabledToast: Plugin "{name}" was auto-disabled after repeated failures. Re-enable it from Settings → Extensions → Plugins.
duplicateTorrentToast: This torrent is already in task "{name}" — not added again
duplicateTorrentToastUnnamed: This torrent already exists in another task — not added again
componentsFfmpegDesc: Open-source audio/video toolkit. FluxDown uses it to merge separate audio and video tracks from DASH and similar streaming downloads.
componentsYtdlpDesc: Media extractor. FluxDown plugins use it to pull direct media URLs from 1000+ sites (YouTube, etc.) for the download engine.
componentsStatusNotFound: {name} not found. Install it below or specify a path manually.
componentsStatusNotFoundUnsupported: {name} not found. Add it to your system PATH or specify a path manually below.
componentsManagedUnsupported: Managed install isn't available on this platform (e.g. Alpine/OpenWrt musl libc). Use a {name} from your system package manager / PATH, or set a manual path above.
componentsManualPathDesc: Point directly to a {name} executable; takes priority over the managed install and system PATH.
componentsInstallSectionDescFfmpeg: Downloads a static FFmpeg build from the official BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds release on demand — not bundled with the installer.
componentsInstallSectionDescYtdlp: Downloads the official platform binary from the yt-dlp/yt-dlp GitHub release on demand — not bundled with the installer.
componentsUninstallConfirmMsg: This removes the managed {name} build. Manual and system-PATH {name} are not affected.
btSeedMaxActiveDesc: Maximum number of tasks seeding at the same time (0 = unlimited). Completed tasks beyond the limit are queued for seeding.
btAutoReseedDesc: Automatically continue seeding completed tasks after restart, unless seeding was stopped manually
btSeedEnabledDesc: Automatically start seeding when a BT task finishes downloading. Turn off to stop seeding immediately upon completion. Seeding keeps the disk awake, which may stop a NAS or external drive from sleeping
btSeedUploadLimitHint: Upload limit takes effect the next time the task starts or seeding is remounted
manifestTreeEmpty: No matching files — adjust the filter or search
manifestAdvancedHint: Proxy · UA · cookies · headers · threads — group-level, applied to every sub-task
manifestProxyHint: Leave blank to use the global setting
manifestIgnoreTlsHint: Accepts expired or self-signed certificates for this group's sub-tasks only; downloads may be exposed to man-in-the-middle interception.
manifestCookieHint: Usually required for cloud-drive logins (leave blank to send none)
manifestHeadersHint: Extra HTTP headers applied to the whole group (use the Cookie field above for cookies)
groupMemberExpiredResolve: Direct link expired · will re-resolve automatically on next launch ↻
groupDetailLazyRenewHint: Lazy renewal: link re-resolves automatically on every launch
showSidebarRssDesc: Show the RSS subscriptions section in the sidebar
rssSidebarEmptyHint: No subscriptions yet — click + and paste a feed URL.
rssInvalidNumber: Enter a valid number within the allowed range.
rssInvalidSizeRange: Maximum size cannot be smaller than minimum size.
rssValidateBeforeSave: Verify the current feed before subscribing.
rssEditorAuthHint: For feeds requiring cookies or a proxy, configure them under Advanced before verifying.
rssDeleteConfirmDesc: Delete "{name}"? Its item history is removed, but downloads already created are kept.
rssEmptyDesc: Items from the first fetch are marked as read; only items appearing afterwards are downloaded automatically.
rssEmptyFetchingHint: Running the first fetch. This usually takes a few seconds; slow origins or proxied feeds take longer.
rssEmptyErrorHint: The fetch did not complete. Check that the feed URL is reachable; sites that require a login need a cookie under Advanced, and unreachable hosts need a dedicated proxy.
rssNameHint: Leave empty to use the feed title
rssIntervalHint: Fetches that find new items write to disk and may wake a sleeping NAS drive; use a longer interval if that matters
rssProviderPluginHint: This source will be fetched by the selected plugin. Configure the plugin under Settings > Plugins; no extra subscription entry is required.
rssEnabledDesc: Disabling keeps the settings and history but stops fetching.
rssAutoDownloadDesc: Off = collect only: items are listed for you to pick by hand.
rssStartPausedDesc: Tasks are created but do not start, so they take no concurrency slot.
rssUseRegexDesc: Include/exclude are parsed as Rust regex. An invalid pattern lets everything through.
rssSmartEpisodeDesc: Recognises S01E02 / 1x02 / - 02 / 第02话 and keeps one release per episode. Unrecognised titles pass through.
rssPreviewHeader: Rule preview — live against {n} cached item(s)
rssPreviewEmpty: No cached items yet — fetch once to preview the rules.
rssSendRefererDesc: Attaches the feed site as Referer; some private trackers require it.
rssNotifyDesc: One batched notification per fetch, not one per item.
rssWizardStep2: Step 2 of 2 — where do the downloads go?
rssWizardUrlNote: Private feeds with a token in the URL work as-is. Feeds needing cookies can be configured afterwards under Manage subscription · Advanced.
rssWizardSeedNote: Items already in the feed are marked as read; only items published after subscribing are downloaded automatically.
webhookEmptyDesc: Send HTTP notifications to your services when download events happen.
webhookDialogDesc: Task events are pushed to your endpoint over HTTP POST — pick a service preset and the payload format is generated for you.
webhookUrlHint: Paste the push URL the service gave you
webhookUrlHintNtfy: The URL must include the topic path, e.g. https://ntfy.sh/my-topic
webhookUrlWarnHttp: Plaintext HTTP — turn on “Allow plaintext HTTP” under Advanced
webhookUrlInvalid: This is not a valid http(s) URL
webhookEventsEmpty: No events selected — this endpoint will never fire
webhookTemplateHint: Leave empty to use the preset default. Placeholder substitution only — no conditions, no loops.
webhookSignDesc: Adds an X-FluxDown-Signature header (t=timestamp,v1=digest) so the receiver can verify origin and reject replays.
webhookAllowHttpDesc: Only recommended for LAN devices (Home Assistant, NAS…).
webhookUseProxyDesc: Off by default — forcing a LAN endpoint through a proxy always fails. Turn it on for services that need one (Telegram, Discord…).
webhookPreviewMeta:
Any 2xx = success · 10s timeout per attempt
Network errors and 5xx retry 3× (2s/4s/8s)
4xx is not retried (treated as a config error)
Deliveries to one endpoint are serialised, preserving order
webhookLogSimulateHint: Pushes a sample event through each endpoint’s real subscription rules — no actual download needed.
webhookLogHint4xx: 4xx is treated as a configuration error and is not retried — check whether the webhook still exists on the server.
webhookSimulateNoTarget: No target subscribes to task.completed — nothing was sent.
webhookSimulateDispatched: Queued for {n} endpoint(s). Delivery results will appear in the log.
doctorDesc: Check browser extension registration, local services, protocol handlers and the log directory
doctorCopied: Report copied — paste it straight into your feedback
doctorRepairOk: NMH registration rewritten — restart your browser for it to take effect
doctorNmhLogEmpty: No relay log yet — the browser extension has never connected
doctorHintReinstallApp: Reinstall FluxDown — part of the installation is missing
doctorHintReregisterNmh: Hit “Re-register” on this row, then restart your browser
doctorHintNmhOtherInstall: The extension works: another FluxDown installation serves it, and a browser cold start launches that installation. Hit “Use this installation” to switch
doctorHintRestartApp: Hit “Restart listener” on this row; if it still fails, restart FluxDown
doctorHintEnableLocalServer: Hit “Enable service” on this row, or turn it on under Settings › API Service
doctorHintCheckFirewall: Check whether a firewall or security suite is blocking the local port
doctorHintEnableProtocol: Hit “Register” on this row, or enable the association under Settings › General
doctorHintProtocolClaimed: Another app owns this protocol — hit “Register” on this row to take it back
doctorHintAssociationOff: Turned off under Settings › General. No other app on this system can take it over, so the system still hands it to FluxDown, which ignores it
doctorHintCheckDisk: Check free disk space and write permissions on the folder
doctorListenerRestartOk: Local listener restarted — reconnect from the browser extension
autoResumeOnStartDesc: Automatically continue tasks that were downloading when the app was last closed
localServiceInvalidArgument: The value was rejected by the local service
apiServiceLanRestartHint: Takes effect the next time the local service starts
webLogoutDesc: Clears the access key saved in this browser, disconnects, and returns to the sign-in page.
btMseModeDesc: Disabled: plaintext only · Enabled: prefer encrypted, accept plaintext · Forced: encrypted peers only
doctorHintDaemonStartupFailed: The download daemon keeps exiting right after launch — usually its local port (17801) is unavailable or another process holds the data directory. Check the stderr excerpt above and fluxdownd.stderr.log, then restart FluxDown
doctorHintDiskSleepBlockers: Seeding, RSS auto-fetch and idle file scan keep touching the disk while idle, which can stop a NAS disk from spinning down. Pause or stop seeding, disable or lengthen RSS sources, or turn idle file scan off if you want the disk to sleep
doctorHintDirPermission: FluxDown cannot write to this folder. Click "Fix permissions" to give write access back to the current user (if the folder belongs to another user, administrator authorization is requested and only this folder is changed). Without that button (for example Docker / NAS), check the folder owner and permissions; for Docker, check PUID/PGID and the volume mount. If it still fails on Windows, Controlled Folder Access may be blocking it: allow FluxDown in Windows Security
doctorHintDirPermissionMacos: macOS privacy protection blocked the write. Click "Open System Settings" and allow FluxDown in Privacy & Security › Files and Folders (other locations need Full Disk Access), then run the diagnostics again
doctorHintDirReadOnly: The disk holding this folder is mounted read-only. Remount it read-write or choose another folder
doctorHintLowDiskSpace: Not enough free space: large files and BT tasks will fail. Free up space or choose a folder on a larger disk
doctorHintDirMissing: Neither the folder nor its parents exist. Make sure the external or network drive is connected, or choose the folder again in Settings
doctorHintDirTimeout: The disk did not respond in time. Check the network drive connection or the disk's health
doctorHintComponentBlocked: The system refused to run this program. Check its execute permission and mount options (noexec); on macOS remove the quarantine attribute or allow it in Privacy & Security; on Windows check whether security software blocks it; or reinstall it in Settings › Components
doctorHintComponentBlockedFixable: The system refused to run this component installed by FluxDown. Click "Fix execute permission"; if it still fails, the data folder may be mounted with noexec or security software may block it — reinstall it in Settings › Components
doctorHintPermissionProbeFailed: The download service did not finish the folder and component checks in time. Restart FluxDown and run the diagnostics again
doctorHintComponentBroken: The program starts but fails (corrupted file, wrong architecture or missing libraries). Reinstall it or pick another version in Settings › Components
doctorHintAutostartBlocked: Launch at startup is disabled by the system. Click "Re-enable" to restore it; if that does not help, enable it in Windows Settings › Apps › Startup or Task Manager, in macOS System Settings › General › Login Items, or in your desktop environment's autostart settings
doctorHintNotificationsBlocked: The system has turned off FluxDown notifications. Click "Open System Settings", allow FluxDown in the notification settings, then run the diagnostics again
doctorHintNotificationsUnavailable: This session has no notification service (no notification daemon is running), so download notifications will not appear
doctorHintNotificationsUnverified: The system does not expose notification permission. Click "Send test notification"; if nothing appears, allow "Script Editor" in System Settings › Notifications
doctorTestNotificationBody: If you can see this, download notifications work.
doctorHintNmhLaunchFailed: Launching the relay the way a browser does failed, so the browser extension cannot connect. Click "Re-register" to rewrite the registration (administrator authorization is requested if old files must be given back to you); if it still fails, check security software or reinstall FluxDown
doctorHintNmhPolicyBlocked: An organization policy (NativeMessagingBlocklist) blocks FluxDown's native messaging host. This is an administrator setting that FluxDown does not bypass; ask IT to allow com.fluxdown.nmh
doctorHintNmhUserHostsDisabled: An organization policy (NativeMessagingUserLevelHosts) disables per-user native messaging hosts, so the browser ignores FluxDown's registration. This is an administrator setting that FluxDown does not bypass; contact IT
doctorHintNmhCmdDisabled: A group policy (DisableCMD) turns off the command prompt, which Chrome / Edge use to start native messaging hosts, so the extension cannot connect. Ask your administrator to set the policy to "No" or to allow scripts
doctorHintNmhForeignOwned: These files belong to another user (usually because FluxDown was once run with sudo), so the registration can no longer be updated automatically. Click "Re-register" and authorize to give them back to the current user
doctorHintRunningElevated: FluxDown is running as root, so every file it writes belongs to root and cannot be changed later by your normal account. Restart FluxDown as your normal user
doctorRepairCancelled: Authorization was cancelled; the changes that needed it were not made
doctorRepairUnavailable: Administrator authorization could not be requested (for example, no polkit authentication agent). Follow the hint for this item to fix it manually
doctorRepairRunningElevated: FluxDown is running as root, so permissions cannot be given back to a normal user. Restart FluxDown as your normal user, then repair
doctorRepairIncomplete: The repair ran, but the check still fails. Follow the hint for this item to continue
doctorRepairNotApplicable: This item cannot be repaired automatically (for example, a system folder or the home folder itself). Follow the hint or choose another folder
doctorTestNotificationSent: Test notification sent; if you did not see it, check the system notification settings
doctorSettingsOpened: System Settings opened; run the diagnostics again after changing it
revealFileCmdShortDesc: Custom command used to reveal files; leave empty for the platform default
showSidebarCategoryNestedDesc: Show category sub-items nested inside the status folders
activityBarSectionDesc: Choose which entries appear in the activity bar; it hides when all optional entries are off
showActivityRssDesc: Show the RSS subscriptions entry in the activity bar
showActivityWebhooksDesc: Show the Webhooks entry in the activity bar
showActivityThemeDesc: Show the light/dark toggle at the bottom of the activity bar
webLoginSubtitle: Enter the access key of this server.
webLoginInvalidKey: Access key rejected. Check it and try again.
webAuthExpired: Your access key is no longer valid. Please sign in again.
webSetupSubtitle: Set an access key to protect this server.
webSetupHint: You will need this key to sign in from any browser. Keep it somewhere safe.
webSetupAlreadyDone: Setup was already completed. Sign in instead.
webKeyBadChars: Use printable ASCII characters only (no spaces).
webKeyNeedsMix: Include at least one letter and one digit.
webReconnecting: Connection to the server was interrupted. Downloads keep running on the server — they don't depend on this browser. Reconnecting…
webReconnectingIn: Connection to the server was interrupted. Downloads keep running on the server — they don't depend on this browser. Reconnecting in {seconds}s (attempt {attempt})…
webIncompatible: This web UI is not compatible with the server version.
webApiBindFixed: In server mode the listen address and port are fixed by FLUXDOWN_BIND
webFsDenied: No permission to read this folder.
webPluginInstallDirHint: Absolute path of the plugin directory on the machine running FluxDown.
webChangeUrlErrTaskActive: Cannot change the link while the task is active
webChangeUrlErrTaskCompleted: Cannot change the link of a completed task
webChangeUrlErrBtUnsupported: BT tasks cannot change their link
webChangeUrlErrProtocolMismatch: The new link must use the same protocol (HTTP/FTP) as the original
cloudSyncStatusHalted: Sync paused: {reason}. Fix the problem, then turn sync off and on again.
syncScopeDesc: Turn a group off to keep it local — it will neither upload nor take cloud values.
downloadToDispatchedOffline: Sent {count} task(s) to {device} — it is offline and will start them once it comes online
downloadToOfflineHint: This device is offline; the task starts once it comes online.
downloadToRemoteOptionsIgnored: Only the links, file name and folder are sent; other advanced options apply on this server only.
downloadToRemoteDirHint: Leave empty to use the target device's default download folder.
downloadToRemoteBrowseDisabled: The folder browser only works for this server; type a path on the target device.
downloadToPathInvalid: Enter an absolute path on the target device, e.g. {example}
webDaemonOffline: The server's download service is offline. The web page is connected, but tasks can't be controlled until it recovers.
errReasonMailNotConfigured: The server can't send email right now. Contact the administrator.
errReasonSessionExpired: Your sign-in has expired. Please sign in again.
errReasonTargetDeviceOffline: The target device is offline, so the command can't be delivered.
errReasonTaskStateConflict: The task's current state doesn't allow this action.
errReasonTaskDeviceMismatch: Only the target device can update this task.
errReasonSaveDirUnavailable: The folder isn't available on the target device. Use an absolute path in its format, or leave it empty.
errReasonPairingCodeInvalid: The pairing code is wrong or has expired.
errReasonPairingSessionExpired: The pairing session has expired. Start again.
errReasonPairingPeerUnreachable: Can't reach that address. Check the address and that both devices are online.
errReasonPairingNotFluxDown: That address isn't a FluxDown service. Check the protocol, port or reverse proxy.
errReasonPairingThrottled: Too many failed attempts. Try again later.
errReasonPairingRejected: The other device rejected the pairing.
errReasonPairingSignatureInvalid: The other device's identity check failed.
errReasonPairingSelf: A device can't pair with itself.
errReasonPairingVersionMismatch: The other device uses an incompatible pairing protocol. Update both devices to the same FluxDown version.
errReasonPeerNotPaired: That device isn't paired (or was unpaired).
localPairingMyCodeHint: Enter this code (and address) on the other device to pair with this one.
localPairingNoAddress: No LAN address is available for this device.
localPairingLanDisabledHint: LAN access is off, so other devices can't reach this one. Turn on LAN access under Settings → Browser integration / Gateway.
localPairingAddressHint: host, host:port, or http(s)://host[:port][/path]. Defaults: http 17800, https 443.
localPairingIncomingDesc: {device} wants to pair with this device. Confirm only if both screens show the same numbers.
linkedDevicesDesc: Devices paired directly, without an account. You can send downloads to them.
linkedDeviceRemoveDesc: {name} will no longer be able to receive downloads from this device.
accountSessionRevokedExpired: You were signed out because your session expired or was revoked. Please sign in again.
accountSessionRevokedUntrusted: This device was removed from your trusted devices, so you were signed out.
accountCodeExpired: Code expired — tap Resend to get a new one
accountErrorDeviceUntrusted: This device is no longer trusted for this account. Please sign in again.
localPairingAddressInvalid: Enter a valid address: host, host:port or http(s)://host[:port]
